# v0.33.0 exact predecessor and append contract

The accepted predecessor is v0.32.0 commit `14d4c26054b77aa4a431a6c1cc0de3458a0c63c1`, tree `342da27ca3d781e55d0153a88171d0b2b3f7dd31`. The new ledger records SHA-256 hashes for all 383 predecessor files and exact UTF-8 byte edits for the explicit changed-existing-file allowlist. Every admitted successor file must match its current byte pin before any reverse edit is applied; reconstructed predecessor bytes must match their independent old pin and round-trip to the admitted successor.

The sole predecessor-chain bridge changes `material_measures_preservation.release_bytes` to call `pre_material_porous_bytes` for bytes that do not match the already pinned v0.32 release. The v0.32 guard obtains its helper bytes through the same exact bridge before checking its unchanged historical helper hash. The complete original helper and guard are independently recoverable through the new ledger. No historical ledger, fixture, snapshot or test declaration is replaced, weakened or regenerated. Runtime modules do not import preservation helpers.

Record collections pin whole objects and their ordered prefixes, including every prior source, identity, grade, state and property. Independent future records may only append after these prefixes. Existing catalog-only claim evidence may retain the older explicitly supported evidence suffix extension; original evidence prefixes and all other fields remain pinned. Executable claims cannot gain evidence through this exception. Catalog envelope metadata and old locale labels remain pinned. A fixed serializer is accepted only for an actual independent append and must still reproduce the exact release byte hash. Reformatting alone is rejected.

README normalization validates live catalog counts and preserves only the previously documented exact historical current-summary intermediate. Outside those count regions, prose stays byte pinned. Disposable mixed append tests refresh their own truthful counts and cannot rewrite frozen release templates or historical scientific fixtures.

The v0.33 admission fixture and four-language detail-output hashes cover source-qualified material states and property views. Old detail-output hashes are generated from the immutable v0.32 source, then compared to the new runtime without rewriting output metadata. New-detail hashes are presentation regression snapshots, not independent scientific validation. Semantic/source transcription fixtures separately establish admitted facts. Source and property identities are retained in each output case so unrelated future additions do not change the accepted scope.
